name: copilot-chat-basics
aliases: why is copilot not reading my file
summary: The foundation guide every other skill assumes. It teaches the handful of moves that make Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat useful and safe for a beginner: opening the right (work) Copilot, attaching or referencing your files, writing a prompt that gets a good answer, and reading the reply critically. If you learn only one guide, learn this one.
use_cases: You are about to run a prompt from this library for the first time and want Copilot set up correctly.; Copilot's answers feel vague or generic and you are not sure it actually read your attachment.; Copilot returned something wrong or invented and you want to sanity-check how you asked.; You are unsure whether you are in the work Copilot or the personal one before pasting company files.

name: copilot-in-excel
summary: How to use Copilot inside Excel for the number-heavy parts of labeling: organizing formula and ingredient tables, scaffolding Nutrition Facts math, and cleaning up messy data from R&D or a co-packer. The theme throughout: Copilot is fast at structure and slow to be trusted on arithmetic, so it drafts the table and you verify every number.
use_cases: You inherited an R&D or supplier spreadsheet and need to understand its columns and formulas before trusting it.; You want to scaffold servings-per-container or percent-of-RACC arithmetic before a Nutrition Facts Panel buildout.; You need to clean up messy formula or nutrient data (inconsistent units, blank cells) into a proper table.; You have nutrient data to summarize or check before handing off to [[nutrition-facts-panel-buildout]] and [[nutrition-facts-panel-rounding-check]].; Copilot's answers feel off and you want to confirm it is reading the table by column name.

name: copilot-in-outlook
summary: How to use Copilot inside Outlook to draft and reply to email in your voice, summarize long threads, and pull action items, without ever letting it send on its own. Email is where a regulatory position becomes externally consequential, so this guide pairs the convenience with the checks that keep a draft from going out wrong.
use_cases: You are drafting a new email or a reply that states a regulatory position and want it in your own voice.; You need to catch up on a long thread and see what was decided and what is still open.; You want to turn a thread into a saved action list with owners via [[email-thread-to-actions]].; You have a draft and want Copilot to coach its tone and clarity before you send it.; A position email needs its citations checked and its AI assistance kept out of the message body.

name: copilot-in-sharepoint
aliases: find the current label of record
summary: How to use Copilot with SharePoint to find the current label of record, ask questions grounded in a document library, and (where your permissions allow) stand up a site-scoped agent so Copilot answers only from a trusted set of files. SharePoint is where the authoritative documents live, so getting Copilot to point at the right library, and knowing when it cannot, is the whole skill.
use_cases: You are hunting for the current approved label of record or spec in a SharePoint library.; You want to ask questions grounded in a specific file or document library without outside knowledge.; You need to confirm the version and last-modified date of a document before treating it as authoritative.; You want to stand up a site-scoped agent so your team gets answers only from approved files (see [[copilot-layering-reference]]).; You are unsure whether agent creation is enabled for you and need to check with IT before relying on it.

name: copilot-in-word
summary: How to use Copilot inside Word to draft and edit the documents a labeling specialist produces: label copy decks, regulatory memos, and review write-ups, plus comparing two versions of a document. Word is a comfortable place to draft, but comparing long documents is a task where Copilot silently misses things, so this guide points you to the dedicated comparison prompts for anything that matters.
use_cases: You are drafting a regulatory memo or a label copy deck from an outline or a set of points.; You want to tighten or reformat an existing document without changing any number, name, or citation.; You need a first look at what changed between two versions of a document before a full comparison.; You are preparing to run [[production-vs-documented-comparison]] or [[change-propagation-audit]] and want a rough diff first.; You want a long document summarized to its key points.
